_description: Go Expert Configuration for gludd — linter config, test conventions, build flags, module naming, version policy. Map to common project types (CLI, web server, library, gRPC service, Lambda).

conventions.parallel: t.Parallel() at top of test (not in subtests unless isolated)
conventions.cleanup: t.Cleanup() over defer in test helpers

tags.debug: enables debug logging and profiling endpoints

rules: Lowercase only — no underscores, no mixedCase in module path
Sub-modules live in subdirectories (no separate repos for Go projects)
Internal packages use internal/ directory (compiler-enforced privacy)
Public packages go in pkg/ or repository root

conventions.go_mod: Commit go.mod AND go.sum — both are required for reproducible builds
conventions.go_work: DO NOT commit go.work — local-only workspace file
conventions.vendor: Optional — commit vendor/ for air-gapped builds or hermetic CI

language.support_window: Latest stable + previous stable major release

modules.incompatible_major: For v2+, module path MUST include /vN suffix: github.com/org/pkg/v2

web_server.build: CGO_ENABLED=0 static binary for distroless/scratch container

library.test_extra: examples as testable code (go test on examples/)
library.release: Semver tag — GitHub Actions runs tests on tag push

grpc_service.test_extra: buf lint + buf breaking, grpc test server with bufconn

lambda.description: AWS Lambda function (or Google Cloud Function)
lambda.test_extra: lambda.Start(handler) — test handler directly without lambda runtime
lambda.release: Terraform or CDK deploys the zip/container

required_checks: Run gosec (via golangci-lint) on every CI run
Run govulncheck on every CI run (vulnerability database)
Use crypto/rand for all cryptographic randomness (never math/rand)
Use parameterized SQL queries (never string concatenation)
Use html/template (never text/template with user input)
Use securejoin or filepath validation for user-supplied paths
forbidden: encoding/gob with untrusted input (RCE risk via interface decoding)
unsafe package unless absolutely necessary and documented
text/template for HTML output with user-controlled data
reflect to bypass unexported-field protections in security boundaries

error_handling: Always check errors — never _ discard them
Wrap errors with fmt.Errorf(...: %w, err) to preserve chain
Use errors.Is for sentinel checks, errors.As for type extraction
Define custom error types for structured error data
Opaque errors: expose behavior (interfaces), not concrete types
Panic only for truly unrecoverable programmer errors
concurrency: Pass context.Context as first parameter to all blocking functions
Never store context in a struct — pass it explicitly
Use errgroup for concurrent operations that should fail together
Use sync.WaitGroup to wait for goroutine completion
Only the sender closes a channel — never the receiver
Use select with context.Done() for cancellation
Prefer channels or errgroup over sync.Cond
interfaces: Define interfaces at the call site, not the implementation site
Check for nil interface (type=nil, value=nil) before using
resources: Use defer for cleanup immediately after acquiring the resource
Close HTTP response bodies: defer resp.Body.Close()
Use t.Cleanup() (or m.Cleanup() in benchmarks) over defer in tests
Set timeouts on all network operations (http.Client.Timeout, grpc dial timeout)
Use connection pooling — don't open a new connection per request
